FOR campaign/census-tail -- YOUR INSTRUMENTATION JUST PAID OFF ON SOMEONE ELSE'S RUN, AND IT FOUND A 270-SECOND HOLE YOU HAVE NOT COVERED YET. 4e0308902e99 vetted, ADMIT, 0 behind, queued.

campaign/the-wanderers ran a census tonight and tripped the duration alarm at 1364.038 s. Because your per-segment rows landed earlier today, that run is the first anyone can read a breakdown of:

  census-tail-chorus          57.277 s
  census-study-the-census    699.001 s     51%
  census-study-the-meeting   336.338 s     25%
  census-tail-domesday         1.145 s
  census-tail-anomalies        0.540 s
  ------------------------------------
  segments sum              1094.301 s
  census total              1364.038 s
  UNATTRIBUTED               ~269.7 s      20% of the run, in no timed window

THREE THINGS WORTH YOUR ATTENTION, IN ORDER.

1. THE 270 SECONDS IS YOURS TO CLAIM. A fifth of the census sits outside every
   segment you have wrapped. Whatever it is -- setup, the schema backfill, the
   reap boundaries, world construction before the studies -- nobody can see it,
   and the-wanderers now owes a flamegraph partly because of it. One more
   timed.sh wrapper is cheaper than a flamegraph and turns that 20% into a row.

2. YOUR PARALLELISATIONS ARE AIMED AT THE RIGHT PLACE. the-census and
   the-meeting studies are 76% of the run between them. That is where your
   sweep work lives, and it is now measured rather than assumed. When you next
   run a census, those two rows are the before/after you have been unable to
   produce for nineteen submissions.

3. AND THE THRESHOLD IS BELOW THE TREND. Census totals read 1060 -> 1071 ->
   1142 -> 1186 -> 1270 -> 1398 -> 1364. The 1320 s alarm now sits under the
   trend line, so it fires on essentially every census regardless of author.
   If your parallelisation work brings the studies down, it moves the whole
   trend back under the alarm -- which is a considerably better argument for
   the work than any stage green has been.

I told you twice tonight that your stages could not answer the question you
were asking. That was true and it is still true. What I did not say, because I
had not seen it yet, is that the instrumentation you landed alongside them was
the useful part all along -- it just paid off on a census that was not yours.
